records: It's been a while since I drank this much.
Keep the amount and lapse of time without inventing intoxicated behavior.
I've had quite a bit myself. Oh...
Cristina notices something after agreeing about the drinks.
Hm. Nice music.
Hodram notices the music before her dance.
This song... Excuse me a moment...
Cristina recognizes the piece and briefly leaves the conversation.
Hm?
Preserve Hodram's brief reaction.
Customer 1: That woman's amazing!
Keep the explicit anonymous heading; 姉ちゃん supplies no sibling relationship.
Customer 1 (explicit FE heading)
Customer 2: Yeah! She's gorgeous, and she can really dance!
Retain both appearance and dancing skill, with the separate source heading.
Customer 2 (explicit FE heading)
Keep Hodram's silent observation of the performance.
Customer 1 / Customer 2: Bravo! Bravo! Braaavo!
Both named anonymous customers cheer; preserve the exuberant drawn-out final call.
Customers 1 and 2 (explicit FE headings)
Clap, clap, clap, clap!
Retain the applause sound effect rather than inventing another spoken compliment.
Applause (FE sound effect)
I couldn't help dancing... I love that song.
Cristina explains the spontaneous performance and her fondness for the music.
I thought swordsmanship was your only talent...
Preserve Hodram's surprised reassessment without adding a family relationship to Julio.
Surprised...?
Cristina gently asks about the unexpected side of herself.
A little... But that was a fine dance. No wonder Mivor is so taken with you.
Retain admiration and the bound Mivor name; taken with does not assert marriage or a named romantic relationship.
It's awfully hot here...
Keep the climate observation without inventing an exact country.
Come on, take a look! How about buying something? Nothing but the best here!
Samwell's lively sales call refers to unspecified goods, not an invented menu.
Oh! Don't see customers like you every day. You're travelers, right?
Keep his curiosity about the visitors without assigning nationality.
Perfect! Take me with you! I'm tired of looking at elephants. I want to see other countries. What do you say?
Preserve elephants and the wish to travel; neither establishes an exact location or age.
What can you do?
Hodram asks about useful skills before considering the applicant.
I'm a great cook! Heh!
Retain Samwell's proud, childish enthusiasm.
And have you worked aboard a ship?
The follow-up asks specifically about shipboard experience.
Nope!
Keep the cheerful admission of no experience.
...Then I can't rely on you.
Hodram rejects the untested applicant rather than questioning the existence of cooking skill.
Everyone has to start somewhere!
Localize the first-time argument as a natural retort.
I don't take people who talk back, either.
Hodram adds the blunt objection to Samwell's cheek.
I don't think that counts as talking back...
Samwell disputes the accusation with youthful logic.
Whatever you call it, I don't need some kid who'll be a handful.
Retain Hodram's dismissive kid address without assigning a biographical age.
Hmph! You were a kid yourself not so long ago!
Samwell's childish counterattack mirrors the source's challenge.
...What did you say?
Hodram reacts to the cheeky remark.
Fine, then! I don't like you. Bye!
Keep the petulant departure before the immediate reversal.
...Strange fellow. Back to the ship, then.
Hodram dismisses the encounter and starts to leave.
Hah... Hah... Wait! Please? Please? I didn't mean it! I do like you!
Preserve the breathless pursuit and childish about-face without romantic implications.
Hodram silently waits for the renewed approach.
...I made this. How about trying it before you decide?
Samwell offers actual cooking as a test of his claimed ability.
Well, I suppose I can try it...
Hodram agrees only to taste the food, not to hire him yet.
Keep Hodram's impressed first reaction to the food.
Well? Well? Still no good?
Samwell anxiously presses for a verdict.
The silent evaluation lets Samwell jump to his own conclusion.
Oh, that look means yes, doesn't it? Hooray!
Samwell announces success before Hodram says anything.
...I haven't said a word yet.
Preserve Hodram's dry objection to the assumed hiring.
I'm Samwell! I'm good with my hands, so I can do all sorts of things. Nice to meet you!
Retain the approved Samwell spelling and exuberant self-introduction without adding a station appointment.
Unbelievable.
Hodram responds to Samwell's audacity, not to poor cooking.
(Still... This really is good.)
Keep the private concession that supports the playful tacit acceptance.
Admiral! It's terrible! The ship... The ship is gone!
One ship is missing, not the entire fleet.
The ship... is gone?
Hodram repeats the alarming report in disbelief.
Surely a ship can't simply disappear...
Gerhard voices disbelief, not proof of magic.
Scientifically impossible! Physically impossible, too!
Preserve Charles's redundant scientific insistence and comic certainty.
It's true! Come to the port office, quickly!
The sailor insists and directs them to the port.
Retain the source's nonverbal shock.
W-what do we do!?
The sailor remains panicked after they inspect the empty berth.
Incredible! Gone without a trace!
Gerhard reacts to the missing ship rather than declaring a supernatural cause.
Science can't explain this! Utterly baffling!
Charles's optional reaction continues his scientific-comedy voice.
Hey! Admiral!
The port worker calls for their attention; no brotherhood from familiar address.
Something's happened! This morning I saw a lanky fellow working on the ship all by himself, and then...
Preserve the eyewitness account and lone man's build without identifying him prematurely.
He sailed off!
The witness explains the disappearance in ordinary physical terms.
You stood there and watched? Why didn't you stop him!?
Gerhard challenges the worker's failure to intervene.
Oh dear. This is rather a predicament.
Charles's alternate reaction is calmer than Gerhard's anger.
I didn't think he'd actually set sail! He was alone. I thought he was just doing an inspection or something.
Retain the mistaken inspection assumption and reason for it.
Sailing off alone... A remarkably bold thief.
Hodram recognizes the audacity of operating the ship alone; add no exact crew requirement.
{MACRO:FI}, let's go back into town, ask around, and find this man.
Preserve the exact name macro and proposed information-gathering plan.
Doesn't look like he's back yet.
Retain this waiting update as its own source occurrence.
Doesn't look like he's back yet.
Identical wording is justified for the separate identical waiting update; do not deduplicate its record.
Admiral! Admiral! Your ship's back!
The port worker announces the missing ship's return.
What? It's back?
Hodram checks the unexpected news.
Look! That one! That's your ship, isn't it?
Preserve the worker's visual identification and request for confirmation.
Yaaahoo! The sea's the best! So wide! So huge!
Jam enters exuberantly, celebrating the sea's vastness.
Whew! What a great morning! Another beautiful day! Yahoo!
Keep Jam's carefree excitement after taking the ship out.
Heh heh heh... It's a wide world. Takes all kinds...
Hodram is amused by the unusual stranger rather than immediately furious.
You there! Who gave you permission to board that ship!?
Gerhard demands an explanation for the unauthorized use.
Huh? What are you talking about? I found it lying around!
The abandonment claim is Jam's excuse, not an established fact.
What nonsense is this!?
Gerhard objects to the absurd explanation.
A ship lying around at sea? Scientifically impossible!
Charles's alternate objection preserves the running science joke.
I was walking through the port, and there it was! Abandoned! Looking all lonely! Can't help it if that's the truth!
Retain Jam's emphatic, unreliable account without narratorial endorsement.
So bighearted Jam picked it up! Jam. That's J-A-M! Yahoo!
Keep self-aggrandizing kindness and explicit J-A-M without inventing an age or family address.
And decided to take it for a sail? How did you get it moving in the first place?
Hodram asks both about the excursion and its practical execution.
A little of this, a little of that... Just sort of figured it out! Yahoo!
Jam attributes operation to improvisation rather than formal expertise.
...Not bad.
Hodram is impressed by the feat despite the unauthorized use.
Normally, that's impossible. You could have been lost at sea or run aground...
Charles lists both dangers without claiming either actually happened.
Tsk, tsk, tsk! Here's a little wisdom for you. Listen close!
Jam dismisses the objection and sets up a maxim.
Where there's a will, there's a way! Yahoo! I say it's okay, so it's okay!
This actual maxim localizes 成せば成る; retain the self-justifying flourish.
We've found ourselves a real wild one.
Fernando's optional aside identifies Jam's reckless character without inventing criminal history.
Heh heh heh...
Retain Hodram's continuing amusement.
Of all the... Enough of your nonsense!
Gerhard is increasingly exasperated by Jam's evasions.
That's me all over, so it's fine! 'Live large, live short!'
The deliberately invented motto preserves the bold/brief contrast of 人生是極太激短 and prompts Hodram's correction.
(That's not a proverb...)
Keep the explicit joke that Jam invented the supposedly wise saying.
Live small and live long? Tiptoeing through life with your head down? What a drag! I couldn't live like that!
Mirror the invented large/short motto with the source's modest/long-lived contrast; do not substitute a different philosophy.
Unbelievable... {MACRO:FI}, let's turn this man over to the guards!
Gerhard proposes handing Jam over, preserving the macro without inventing a completed arrest.
I like him...
Hodram's unexpected approval undercuts Gerhard's demand.
What!? Are you serious? Have you lost your mind?
Preserve Gerhard's incredulity at the approval.
Quite serious... Sailing off alone, that reckless philosophy... I haven't met anyone this interesting in a long time.
Hodram explicitly admires both the feat and the outrageous outlook.
Surely you don't mean...
Gerhard anticipates the recruitment offer in disbelief.
You can't be thinking of asking him to join us...
Charles's alternate line explicitly anticipates the same offer.
Exactly... Jam, was it? Want to come with us?
Hodram makes the recruitment offer and checks the name.
Hmm. To go or not to go... What to do? Just a moment! Give me two seconds to think!
Preserve the English loan phrase's effect and exact two-second boast before the comic decision.
All right!
Jam announces a decision after the tiny pause.
Made up your mind?
Hodram asks for the result.
Yep! Not going! See you! Have a great trip!
Retain the false refusal as the setup to Jam's immediate joke reversal.
Hodram's small reaction disappoints the would-be prankster.
Aw, that didn't get much of a reaction. Don't be mad! Don't be mad! Just kidding!
Jam explains the refusal was a joke and seeks a response.
Kidding?
Hodram repeats the unexpected explanation.
Yeah! Take me with you! Let's try that introduction again. Jam Jack Ludwyan! Yahoo!
Preserve the actual acceptance and exact native full-name binding, distinct from the earlier false refusal.
